import ctypes
import struct

# Define the C functions manually since they are not part of GSL
# These are mock implementations for demonstration purposes
# In a real scenario, these would be implemented in a C library

# Mock C function for float
def make_float_bigendian_c(value):
    packed = struct.pack('>f', value)  # Big-endian
    unpacked = struct.unpack('>f', packed)[0]  # Convert back
    return unpacked

# Mock C function for double
def make_double_bigendian_c(value):
    packed = struct.pack('>d', value)  # Big-endian
    unpacked = struct.unpack('>d', packed)[0]  # Convert back
    return unpacked

# Python wrapper functions

def make_float_bigendian(value):
    return make_float_bigendian_c(value)


def make_double_bigendian(value):
    return make_double_bigendian_c(value)

    original_float = 1.2345
    big_endian_float = make_float_bigendian(original_float)
    # Verify by manually converting to big-endian and back
    packed = struct.pack('>f', original_float)  # Big-endian
    unpacked = struct.unpack('>f', packed)[0]  # Convert back
    assert big_endian_float == unpacked, f"Failed for float: {original_float}"

    # Test cases for make_double_bigendian
    original_double = 1.23456789
    big_endian_double = make_double_bigendian(original_double)
    # Verify by manually converting to big-endian and back

    unpacked = struct.unpack('>d', packed)[0]  # Convert back
    assert big_endian_double == unpacked, f"Failed for double: {original_double}"
